judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — P1 (89%): The response-parser feature gate is not propagated from the sibling dispatch gate: `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) {`. `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires `userId` (`&& userId` at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5) and therefore leaves team credentials on their provider refresh path, while this code nevertheless forces their provider response through the sync endpoint's minimal response contract. Team-owned Google, Office365, and Salesforce credentials consequently do not retain the ordinary provider-specific parsing behavior whenever sync is merely configured.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic inconsistency. In refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5, the condition is `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId)` - requiring userId to be truthy. However, in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15, the condition is only `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` - it doesn't check userId. This means when credential sync is configured but userId is null (team credentials), refreshOAuthTokens will use the normal refresh path (returning provider-specific response), but parseRefreshTokenResponse will still use minimumTokenResponseSchema instead of the provider-specific schema. This is a real logic bug where the two functions have mismatched conditions.
